source.title: From Indirect Object Identification to Syllogisms: Exploring Binary Mechanisms in Transformer Circuits

record.file_problem: none; the full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: Extends the study of IOI-associated heads to syllogism tasks and reports interventions on GPT-2 small. It does not test IOI performance itself.
record.gate_note: The paper studies syllogisms, not IOI prompts or the IOI circuit as a whole. Its relevant results concern reuse and changed roles of particular heads previously associated with IOI. Syllogism-only circuit faithfulness, binary-token transfer results, and larger-model results are not evidence for the IOI versions unless they specifically test an IOI-associated component.
record.test_reason: The study reverse-engineers GPT-2 small on syllogism prompts. It finds that heads named in the IOI circuit are reused: 10.7 and 11.10 act as negative truth heads; 9.9 and 10.1 act as truth heads; 7.3 and 8.10 act as truth modulation heads, which the authors align with S-Inhibition. This bears on V3's claim that IOI components are reused for other tasks. It does not run IOI prompts.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors report significant overlap with the IOI circuit. Heads labelled negative copy heads in IOI encode the opposite of the attended value in binary settings and so implement negation. Truth modulation heads align with S-Inhibition. They present this as broadening the IOI interpretation, while acknowledging that understanding remains limited.
record.recipe_differences: Uses path patching, as in the IOI analysis, but investigates syllogism prompts and does not evaluate the IOI circuit’s faithfulness, completeness, or minimality.
record.method_sensitivity: Head 10.7 has contrasting effects across the SS and OS prompt formats: ablating it improves SS performance but significantly reduces OS logit difference.

fits_no_version.finding: In larger models (GPT-2 XL, Pythia 1.4B, Qwen3-1.7B, LLaMA3.2-1B), negative-copy heads are present but their effect on syllogism logits is muted. Pythia 1.4B is the exception.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: IOI-type negative-copy heads exist in other models, but their reuse on non-IOI tasks varies by model.

record.problems: The IOI-related evidence is indirect and limited to syllogism tasks; the head-ablation effects are described qualitatively without numeric values or uncertainty estimates.
record.rows_left_out: No additional IOI-linked results were reported. Other syllogism circuit and model-scale results do not directly test the versions’ IOI claims.

untested.parts: No IOI test of the 26-head circuit, its classes, faithfulness, completeness or minimality.
No name-mover ablation on IOI and no measurement of backup heads.
IOI circuits in other models, sizes or checkpoints. The Appendix D larger models are tested on syllogisms only.
No comparison of circuit-finding methods, ablation types or metrics on IOI.
No test of how IOI faithfulness or completeness depends on the evaluation.

missing.what: SS truth heads include 9.9 and 10.1, which overlap with IOI name mover and backup heads. The authors state this overlap.
Truth Modulation Heads 7.3, 8.8 and 8.10 in the complex syllogism. The authors align them with IOI S-Inhibition heads and identify the Correct Truth Inhibition Heads as the original inhibition heads.
Negative truth head 11.10 (an IOI negative name mover) is reused alongside 10.7.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence is indirect: IOI prompts are never run. Head-level effects are given only in figures, with no uncertainty reported. The faithfulness metric is |ALD(M)−ALD(C)|, used on syllogism circuits only, so it does not bear on V1 or V5. One could argue for T5, since the study reinterprets the role of IOI negative heads; T3 is kept because the results come from a new task.

versions.untested_parts: No IOI task test of the 26-head, 7-class circuit, or its faithfulness, completeness, or minimality.
No ablation of IOI name-mover heads to test backup-head self-repair on IOI.

Tests reuse of some IOI-associated heads in GPT-2 small syllogism tasks, but not the IOI circuit across other models, sizes, or checkpoints; nor whether the full set of IOI head classes and roles is shared across tasks.
Does not compare circuit-finding methods, ablation types, or evaluation metrics on IOI.
Does not test how IOI circuit evaluation changes with ablation, metric, or prompt distribution.
Does not test IOI across name orders, templates, or numbers of names.

rows.note: The paper identifies head 10.7 as an IOI-associated negative head, but its removal improves SS performance, so its contribution is not uniformly constructive across tasks.
rows.check: In IOI, 10.7 is a negative head that lowers the correct logit. Mean-ablating it in SS improves performance, so it plays the same negative role in a new task; that is reuse, not a partial effect. The baseline is readable from Table 1: SS average logit difference 1.8575. The size of the improvement is not stated.

relationships.condition: GPT-2 small, syllogism tasks (SS, OS, CS)
relationships.reason: Heads from the IOI circuit are reused in the syllogism circuits. IOI negative head 10.7 hurts SS (R1) and drives OS (R2). The text also reports overlap with name movers and S-Inhibition heads, which no row records.
relationships.display_finding: IOI head 10.7 hurts SS but drives OS, and syllogism circuits also reuse name movers and S-inhibition heads.

source_check.condition: GPT-2 small, syllogism tasks (SS, OS, CS)
source_check.reason: R1 and R2 establish causal involvement of IOI-associated head 10.7 in SS and OS. Sections 3.3 and 4 additionally describe overlap with IOI head classes in CS, although separate rows are missing.

relationships.reason: The reused heads' roles differ from their IOI labels. The authors say negative heads negate rather than copy. Head 10.7's effect flips sign between SS (R1) and OS (R2), so the roles are not identical across tasks.
relationships.display_finding: Head 10.7's contribution reverses sign between SS and OS, and the authors interpret negative heads as performing negation rather than copying.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.reason: R1 and R2 support reuse of the same component across tasks. Its contribution changes sign with the required answer, while suppression remains useful for negation. V3 does not require unchanged roles across non-IOI tasks.

tranche.reason: Causal analysis of syllogism tasks provides results on reuse of IOI-associated components in a new setting.

source_check.notes: The authors_conclusion paraphrase is faithful. Additional rows are needed for the reported Name Mover and S-Inhibition overlap; the paper's qualitative use of significance is not accompanied by uncertainty estimates.

statements.correction: Head 10.7: mean ablation improves SS performance; direct-effect path patching reduces OS logit difference. Appendix C: MLP patching compared with attention restored versus absent. Statistical uncertainty estimates: not reported. Laundry List findings: outside this study's check.
statements.problem: The syllogism intervention findings are correct, but the blanket claim that the paper reports no controls overlooks its controlled patching comparisons.

statements.correction: Head 10.7: detrimental to SS, constructive in OS. Section 4: negative heads interpreted as implementing negation beyond copying. V3 component reuse: supported; invariant roles across non-IOI tasks: not required by the supplied version.
statements.problem: The reported findings and authors' interpretation are accurate, but they do not justify limits_scope for V3, which requires component reuse on other tasks without requiring unchanged roles there.

reader_labels.reason: Ablating the IOI-associated negative-copy head 10.7 significantly reduces logit difference in OS, consistent with reuse of an IOI-associated component in another task (R2).
